citation: J. W. Taylor (Chicago), 'Pullman, George M., Residence', photograph no. 1445, 1890s: album no. 1, p. 69, and print 16399. Art Institute of Chicago, Ryerson and Burnham Archives.
author: J. W. Taylor (Chicago)
describes_date: after the 1892 additions east of the flank (they stand in it); the album print's holder dates it c. 1880s, the album c. 1890s
repository: Art Institute of Chicago, Ryerson and Burnham Archives (https://digital-libraries.artic.edu/digital/collection/mqc/id/38973 and /id/29304). Prairie library images a16-aic-taylor-album-pullman-p69 and a16-aic-taylor-pullman-from-nw; the image store's copies of both are committed at data/sources/assets/pullman_1729_taylor_t3161/.
locator: The whole print: the house from the south-west corner of Prairie Avenue and 18th Street, looking north-east, the Prairie Avenue front with its portico at left and the 18th Street flank running away at right, seen far more squarely than in the Detroit print (about 18 px a metre along it at the corner of the 1200 px album print): its corner pier, one window, the arcaded porte-cochere with its balustraded deck, the windows over it, the great stack on the cornice and the dormers, and the 1892 additions beyond. The camera (data/reference_views/pullman_house_1729_prairie/taylor_1445_album.json) says how far it can be measured.
rights_note: A commercial photograph of the 1890s, public domain by age: the owner's ruling of 2026-10-27 on T-3161 (answer a), as with Taylor's 1801 Kimball print (taylor_c1895_kimball_residence_1801). The Art Institute asks to be contacted for publication. Read for forms, counts, places, heights and proportions; no texture or mesh is derived from it.
access_notes: Read 2026-10-28 (T-3161) from the image store's copies, both committed unaltered: the album print 1200 x 923 px, 171,701 bytes, sha256 8e9acc6fe325b5e7d7aa04c68396fe02cfb8e31b10e55a1a8e9fb8e2b29df345, and print 16399 1200 x 1100 px with the Archives' grey scale, 189,584 bytes, sha256 7e09cff542e8006816e1c37ef2165813df4858e4e76675f68f9dc20964369bb5 (the holder's IIIF 1200 px derivatives). Both carry '1445' on the sidewalk and the same trees, carriage marks and shadows; phase correlation puts 16399 at 1.015 x the album print, offset (-6, +29) px (docs/RESEARCH/photo-match/pullman_house_1729_prairie/taylor-1445-camera.md). The holder's 'view from NW' on 16399 is the content's south-west.
note: The sharpest picture of the 18th Street flank. Read off the album print through its camera: east of the corner pier one round-arched window on each storey; then the porte-cochere, a one-storey block standing about 5.4 m out from the flank with an arch in its west end (the house's side door seen through it) and one in its south front, under an entablature and a balustraded deck; over it on the second storey a pair of narrow round-headed lights, a pier with an oculus, and a triple; on the principal storey east of it a pair seen through the arches; the great stone stack on the cornice just east of the corner pier; three dormers on the flank's mansard, each over a group of windows; and at the flank's east end a section whose cornice breaks forward. Monochrome (a toned print).
what_it_supplies: the 18th Street flank's bays, porte-cochere and dormers
the flank stack and its height
